name: application-no-results-search-state
title: No-Results Search State
description: Search-specific empty view that echoes the real search query back to the user and, when filters are active, offers a real clear-filters action — distinct from the generic empty-states component.
useWhen: A search query returned zero results and the user needs to know exactly what they searched for.
Active filters may be responsible for the empty result set, and clearing them is a real recovery action.
The empty state is a direct consequence of user input (a query), not a generic "no data yet" condition.
avoidWhen: There's no query to echo — e.g. a brand-new list with no data yet — use application-empty-states instead.
The zero-result state is a route-level error, not a search result — use retry-error-state or a 404 page instead.
You need onboarding-style guidance (first-run CTA) rather than a recovery hint — use empty-states' onboarding variant.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a centered block with a max-width message; it reflows naturally at any container width without special breakpoint handling.
accessibility: The search query is rendered as real text (not just implied), so screen readers announce exactly what was searched.
The Clear filters button only renders when hasActiveFilters is true, so it's never a dead/no-op action.
The search icon is decorative (aria-hidden) — the query text and message carry the meaning.

variants.title: No-results search state
variants.description: Zero-result state for the query "wireless keyboard" with active filters and a Clear filters action, on a light surface.
accessibility: The exact query is quoted in visible text so users can confirm what they searched for.

variants.title: No-results search state (Dark)
variants.description: The same zero-result state, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Icon, text, and button colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
